newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Feb 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Feb 12.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Feb. 12:

WASHINGTON - President Clinton and congressional leaders took their first steps toward translating bipartisan words into deeds by agreeing to concentrate on five top priority initiatives in the coming months -- including aid to the District of Columbia.

WASHINGTON - The Federal Election Commission, once hailed as the two-fisted enforcer that would protect the body politic from future Watergate scandals and the corrupting scourge of unregulated campaign cash, has proved to be weak, slow and largely ineffectual.

WASHINGTON - President Clinton seems to have found something of a spititual soul mate in the Rev. Robert Schuller, a television evangelist who preaches about the power of self-esteem and "possibility thinking" to a viewership of millions.

WASHINGTON - A long-time member of Mayor Marion Barry's security detail is the subject of a police investigation into allegations he did not report for duty in his new assignment and that his supervisors were ordered to falsify his time sheets.

WASHINGTON - Former FBI agent Eugene Bennett was convicted of attempted murder by a Manassas jury, which didn't buy his assertion that his wife's affair with crime novelist Patricia Cornwell drove him crazy.

DOLGENBRODT, Germany - When fire engulfed a resort complex here four years ago that was designated as housing for Third World asylum seekers, many people assumed it was just another ugly manifestation of xenophobic hatred perpetrated by skin-heads and right-wing radicals.
BOZEMAN, Mont. - In the sweeping canyon to the north, $300,000 homes creep up the bottom slopes of the Bridger Range, encroaching on habitat for bear, deer and cougar.
